author_or_org: Pratyay Banerjee, Masud Moshtaghi, Ankit Chadha

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: APEX-EM is a non-parametric experience memory that stores complete procedural-episodic traces in a typed Procedural Knowledge Graph (PKG) and retrieves them through semantic search, structural-signature matching over abstract operation sequences, and graph traversal.
claims.quote: We introduce \textbf{APEX-EM}, a non-parametric experience memory that stores complete procedural-episodic traces in a typed Procedural Knowledge Graph (PKG) and retrieves them through three channels: semantic search, structural-signature matching over abstract operation sequences, and graph traversal.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: APEX-EM uses a Plan-Retrieve-Generate-Iterate-Ingest (PRGII) workflow that quality-gates and commits experiences, indexes both successes and failures, and does not change model weights during deployment.
claims.quote: A Plan-Retrieve-Generate-Iterate-Ingest (PRGII) workflow produces, quality-gates, and commits experiences, indexing both successes and failures so the agent learns what to reuse and what to avoid. No weights change during deployment.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The paper evaluates APEX-EM on five benchmarks: BigCodeBench, KGQAGen-10k, HLE, Lifelong Agent Bench, and ALFWorld.
claims.quote: We evaluate on five benchmarks: BigCodeBench, KGQAGen-10k, HLE, Lifelong Agent Bench, and ALFWorld.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Because prior work uses different backbones, the authors base their claims on same-backbone comparisons that hold model capability fixed.
claims.quote: Because prior work uses different backbones, we base our claims on same-backbone comparisons that hold model capability fixed.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: On held-out BigCodeBench transfer with a shared GPT-4o backbone, APEX-EM gains +7.6 pp over the no-memory baseline, which is 3.3 times MemRL's +2.3 pp under the identical setup.
claims.quote: On held-out BigCodeBench transfer with a shared GPT-4o backbone, APEX-EM gains +7.6\,pp over the no-memory baseline, 3.3×MemRL's +2.3\,pp under the identical setup.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: On Lifelong Agent Bench with a shared GPT-4o-mini backbone, APEX-EM gains +1.4 pp for OS and +1.0 pp for DB cumulative success.
claims.quote: On Lifelong Agent Bench with a shared GPT-4o-mini backbone, it gains +1.4\,pp (OS) and +1.0\,pp (DB) cumulative success.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: On KGQAGen-10k, frozen memory transfers to a blind 1,079-question test split at 73.7% versus 42.0% with no memory, approaching an oracle given the ground-truth subgraph at 84.9%.
claims.quote: On KGQAGen-10k, frozen memory transfers to a blind 1{,}079-question test split at 73.7\% versus 42.0\% with no memory, approaching an oracle handed the ground-truth subgraph (84.9\%).

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Component analysis shows no single mechanism dominates: teacher feedback is negligible for code but adds +10.3 pp on structured queries, structural signatures give 3.3 times the transfer of semantic-only retrieval, and within-epoch iteration recovers most of the gain when rich feedback is unavailable.
claims.quote: Component analysis shows no single mechanism dominates: teacher feedback is negligible for code but adds +10.3\,pp on structured queries, structural signatures give 3.3×the transfer of semantic-only retrieval, and within-epoch iteration recovers most of the gain when rich feedback is unavailable.
